title: INC-2026-004: Ransomware on FS-02 via internet-exposed RDP on JMP-01 and the svc.backup service account
severity_rationale: Ransomware activity is confirmed on FS-02: shadow copies were deleted, files were mass-renamed with a .lockd extension, a ransom note was left, and the server had to be restored from offline backup with about 2 days of file changes lost. The 200 GB data-theft claim is not confirmed; egress for FS-02 and JMP-01 showed no large transfers, and other hosts have not been reviewed.
executive_summary: An external IP reached RDP on JMP-01, made 312 failed logons for svc.backup, then logged on successfully. Using svc.backup, the attacker installed a remote service on FS-02, deleted shadow copies and ran locker.exe, which mass-renamed files. A ransom note was left. The root cause was RDP on JMP-01 left open to the internet since 2025 as a temporary vendor exception, and never closed. svc.backup had a 2022 password, no MFA on RDP and admin rights on FS-02, which let one stolen or guessed credential reach the file server. The high-severity shadow-copy alert went to a queue and paged no one. On-call was paged only for the later mass-rename alert. FS-02 and JMP-01 were isolated, svc.backup was disabled and the attacker IP blocked. FS-02 was restored from offline backup with about 2 days of changes lost. The attacker's claim of 200 GB stolen is not confirmed. Egress for FS-02 and JMP-01 showed no large transfers, but other hosts are not yet reviewed, so possible data theft and lateral movement remain open.

what_happened.statement: The firewall allowed connections from external IP 203.0.113.66 to JMP-01 on RDP port 3389.
There were 312 failed RDP logons for svc.backup on JMP-01 from that IP between 22:41 and 22:58, followed by a successful remote interactive logon.

lessons.lesson: Temporary firewall exceptions without an owner and expiry become permanent exposure. A vendor exception stayed open for about a year and was the entry point. Prior guidance on expiring exceptions was not applied here.

corrective_actions.recommendation: Confirm RDP 3389 on JMP-01 is no longer reachable from the internet. Allow remote access only through a bastion or VPN with MFA, and verify this before reconnecting restored systems.
corrective_actions.reason: RDP exposed to the internet was the entry point, and the evidence does not record the exposure being closed.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: opened to the internet in 2025 as a temporary vendor exception and never closed

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: Removes the direct internet attack path to JMP-01.

policy_refs.title: Remote administration
policy_refs.excerpt: Remote administration protocols (RDP, SSH) must never be exposed directly to the internet.

policy_refs.title: Recovery
policy_refs.excerpt: Restore from offline or immutable backups after confirming the entry point is closed

corrective_actions.recommendation: Rebuild svc.backup as least-privilege. Deny interactive and RDP logon, remove local admin on FS-02, and use a long rotated password or a managed identity.
corrective_actions.reason: svc.backup had an old password, no MFA on RDP and admin rights, and was the account used throughout the attack.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: svc.backup had a password last changed in 2022, no MFA on RDP, and admin rights on FS-02

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: A stolen service credential no longer yields remote logon or admin access.

policy_refs.title: Service accounts
policy_refs.excerpt: Service accounts must not be allowed interactive or remote desktop logon.

corrective_actions.recommendation: Audit all existing temporary firewall exceptions. Require a named owner and an automatic expiry of at most 30 days for each, and close those without one.
corrective_actions.reason: The vendor exception had no expiry and stayed open about a year.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: opened to the internet in 2025 as a temporary vendor exception and never closed

corrective_actions.expected_benefit: Prevents other stale exposures from becoming entry points.

open_questions: How did the attacker obtain the svc.backup password? Password guessing after the 312 failures is probable but not confirmed.
Was data actually exfiltrated? Egress for FS-02 and JMP-01 shows no large transfers, but other hosts are not reviewed.
Did the attacker reach other servers from JMP-01?
Is RDP exposure on JMP-01 now closed? The notes record only that svc.backup was disabled and the attacker IP blocked.
Did any alerting fire on the 312 failed RDP logons? The evidence records none.
What is the nature of the 5,320-byte outbound HTTPS connection from FS-02 to 198.51.100.10 at 23:40? Its destination is not identified as malicious in the evidence.
remaining_risks: Possible data theft that has not been ruled out, since egress for other hosts is unreviewed.
Other servers may be compromised via JMP-01.
Other stale temporary exceptions or weak service accounts may exist.
